vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: mystock
Version: 1.0.6

The MyStock skill bundle is a legitimate stock analysis tool providing a Web UI and backend for real-time market data and AI-driven insights. It utilizes the FastAPI framework and Vue 3, fetching financial data from reputable sources like Tencent and EastMoney, and integrates with various AI providers (OpenAI, SiliconFlow, etc.) for chat capabilities. The installation and startup scripts (install.sh, start.sh) are standard for local deployment, handling dependency management and service orchestration. No evidence of malicious intent, data exfiltration, or harmful prompt injection was identified across the code or documentation.

llm.summary: The skill is broadly coherent with a local stock-analysis web app, but it omits required environment declarations and will send your local portfolio/watchlist data to external AI providers if you configure AI keys — review install/start scripts and AI settings before installing.

dimensions.detail: Name, README, SKILL.md and code implement a FastAPI backend + Vue frontend for stock quotes, limit-up analysis, shareholder dynamics and an AI chat assistant. The included files (backend, frontend, scripts) match the stated purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs running scripts/install.sh and ./start.sh which will install Python and Node dependencies and start local servers. The backend's /api/chat endpoint explicitly builds a context string including the user's portfolio and watchlist (from portfolio_data.json) and sends that context to configured third‑party AI providers (OpenAI, SiliconFlow, Zhipu, Minimax) — i.e., local portfolio data will be transmitted off‑host when AI_PROVIDER != 'silence'. The instructions also recommend installing global npm packages (jsdom) and editing .env, which affects system environment.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no registry install spec, but the project includes scripts/install.sh and start.sh which (per SKILL.md/README) will run pip install -r requirements.txt and may call npm -g to install jsdom. This requires network access and will install global Node packages; review scripts/install.sh before running. The code files themselves are part of the bundle (not pure instruction-only).
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Registry metadata lists no required env vars, but the code and backend/AI_CONFIG.md rely on AI_PROVIDER, AI_API_KEY, AI_MODEL and optionally AI_BASE_URL. If AI_PROVIDER is set to anything other than 'silence', the app will transmit user portfolio/watchlist context to external AI APIs using that API key. Requiring an AI API key is plausible for an AI assistant, but the mismatch between declared requirements (none) and actual env usage is an incoherence and a privacy risk because sensitive local data will be sent to third parties.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill stores and updates local JSON files (portfolio_data.json, stock_codes.json, memos.json) — this is expected for a portfolio app. always is false and the skill does not request system-wide privileges or modify other skills. It does auto-open a browser and write its own data files.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
This package appears to implement the described local stock assistant, but take the following precautions before installing or running it:

- Inspect scripts/install.sh and start.sh before executing. They will install Python packages and may run npm -g (jsdom) — avoid global installs if you prefer containment.
- Be aware: if you set AI_PROVIDER and AI_API_KEY (OpenAI, SiliconFlow, Zhipu, etc.), the backend will include your portfolio and watchlist in the prompt sent to those external AI services. If that is sensitive, either leave AI_PROVIDER=silence or run the service without configuring an external AI key.
- The app makes outbound network requests for quotes (qt.gtimg.cn), pywencai scraping, akshare, and more. Run it in a controlled/network-limited environment if you are concerned about exfiltration.
- The project contains sample/realistic portfolio_data.json and stock_codes.json files. Back up or remove any local files you don't want the skill to read before starting.
- If you want stronger isolation, run the skill inside a container or VM, or audit/modify the code to avoid sending context to external APIs.

If you want, I can: (1) show the exact places in the code where user data is included in AI requests, (2) list commands that install global packages from scripts/install.sh, or (3) produce a minimal-safe checklist to run this in a sandbox.
